The inspector's car was already turning into the clinic lane, and the power had been off since noon. Sangeeta Ma'am pushed the vaccine fridge log at Lakshmi. 'Three days are blank. Just fill in the usual reading with last week's dates. Quickly.'
Lakshmi's heart hammered. She was eleven days into the job.
'Ma'am, I can't write readings I didn't take,' she said. 'If the fridge was off, the inspector needs to know, for the vaccines' sake.'
'We'll look careless.'
'We can write today's reading now and add a note that the entries were missed and why. And I'll set a phone reminder so it doesn't happen again.'
Sangeeta Ma'am stared at her, then at the car door slamming outside. 'Fine. Write the note. Fast.'
Lakshmi wrote it in her neatest hand, fingers barely shaking.

qa.q: How many days of the log were blank?
qa.a: Three days were blank.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi feeling as she refused?
qa.a: Her heart hammered because she was new and nervous about refusing a senior, but she was clear she couldn't write readings she hadn't taken.

qa.q: What made Lakshmi's refusal work under pressure?
qa.a: She gave one simple reason and offered an honest alternative, today's reading plus a note and a reminder, so her senior had a quick way forward without backdating.

qa.q: What might Sangeeta Ma'am be feeling as the inspector's car door slams?
qa.a: She is likely anxious about looking careless and irritated at first, but accepts the note because it is honest, quick and she has little time.

grounding: It shows a new hire refusing to backdate a log under time pressure, giving a simple reason and offering an honest alternative.

Kavitha had been at the Chennai design office for three weeks when Ayesha, the senior engineer, slid a site inspection form across her desk.
'Sign this and date it Friday. The client's asking why it's late.'
'Did someone inspect the scaffolding on Friday?'
Ayesha sighed. 'It's the same scaffolding it was on Thursday. It's a formality.'
Kavitha's pulse jumped, but her voice stayed even. 'I can't put a date on something I didn't see. But I can go to the site at seven tomorrow, check it properly and sign it with tomorrow's date. I'll email the client tonight that it's scheduled.'
Ayesha looked at her for a long moment. 'You'll really go at seven?'
'I'll send you a photo from the gate.'
Ayesha took the form back. 'Fine. Seven.'

qa.q: What date did Ayesha want on the form?
qa.a: Ayesha wanted it dated Friday.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling when answering Ayesha?
qa.a: Kavitha's pulse jumped with nerves at refusing a senior, but the voice stayed even and firm about not signing for something unseen.

qa.q: Why is refusing at this first request easier than refusing later?
qa.a: Declining now, with a clear reason and an honest plan, sets Kavitha's line before the shortcut becomes a habit that would be harder to break.

qa.q: How might Ayesha see the new hire after this exchange?
qa.a: Ayesha may be surprised and a little annoyed, but also sees that Kavitha is reliable and is solving the client's problem honestly.

grounding: It shows a new engineer declining to backdate an inspection form, stating the reason plainly and offering a compliant alternative.

"Just date it the twenty-eighth," Sumit said, sliding the delivery receipt across. "Month-end closed on the thirtieth."
"It came in today, though," Samir said. "The second."
"Everyone does it. Otherwise last month's numbers look bad."
Samir looked at the receipt, then at Sumit. His heart was thumping; he had been here three weeks. "I'm not comfortable writing a date that isn't true. If there's an audit, it's my signature."
"Arre, relax."
"I'm not trying to make trouble. What if I date it today and add a note: ordered on the twenty-sixth, delivered late by the vendor? Then the delay's on record, and it's honest."
Sumit frowned. "The manager won't like it."
"I'll explain it to the manager myself, if you want."
Sumit took the receipt back, read it again and sighed. "Fine. Write your note. Actually, send me the format. That vendor's always late."

qa.q: When did the delivery actually come in?
qa.a: The second.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling when he refused to backdate?
qa.a: He felt nervous, heart thumping as a new hire, but firm about not signing a false date.

qa.q: What made Samir's refusal effective?
qa.a: He stated the reason simply, offered an honest alternative with a note on the vendor delay, and offered to explain it himself.

qa.q: How does Sumit's view shift by the end?
qa.a: Sumit moves from pressuring Samir to seeing the note as useful, even asking for the format.

grounding: A new hire declines to backdate a receipt, gives a simple reason and offers an honest alternative, drawing the line at the first bend.

passage:
In my second week at the NGO, Urmila, my senior, handed me a stack of attendance forms for our tailoring training. "Fill in last month's dates. The funder's report is due Friday, and we lost the sheets in the rain."
I remember how easy it would have been. Everyone was busy. Urmila had been kind to me. It was only paperwork.
But I also remembered my first boss saying that the first time is the only easy time to say no.
So I said, "I can't write dates for sessions I didn't see. But I can call the trainees tomorrow, confirm who came, and we can attach a note to the funder about the lost sheets."
Urmila stared at me, then laughed. "That's more work."
"It's honest work."
We spent Thursday on the phone with twenty-six women. Twenty-two confirmed. The funder thanked us for the note. I'm Elizabeth. That was the first bend, and I'm glad I didn't take it.

qa.q: Why were the attendance sheets missing?
qa.a: We lost the sheets in the rain.

qa.q: How did Elizabeth feel when handed the forms?
qa.a: Elizabeth felt tempted and a bit torn, since it seemed easy and Urmila had been kind.

qa.q: What honest alternative did Elizabeth offer?
qa.a: Calling the trainees to confirm attendance and attaching an honest note to the funder about the lost sheets.

qa.q: How might Urmila feel when the funder thanked them?
qa.a: Urmila likely felt relieved and perhaps a little proud of the honest approach.

grounding: A new hire declines to fill in dates for unseen sessions, explains simply and offers an honest alternative.

Lab supervisor's note, week 3 of Mridul's probation
Worth recording. On Tuesday, Rafiq, one of our longest-serving technicians, asked Mridul to backdate the calibration record for the pH meter, which had been missed on Friday. Rafiq told him, "It's always been done this way before the monthly check."
Mridul told Rafiq politely that he couldn't sign a date for a calibration he hadn't seen. Then he offered to run the calibration right then, record today's date, and log Friday's miss in the deviation register. He did exactly that, in twenty minutes.
Rafiq came to me afterwards, a bit annoyed. I told him Mridul had done it correctly and that a logged deviation is far better than a false record.
Actions: I have reminded all staff that missed checks go in the deviation register, without blame, and I thanked Mridul at the team meeting.

qa.q: Which instrument's calibration was missed?
qa.a: The pH meter.

qa.q: What might Mridul have felt refusing a long-serving technician?
qa.a: He probably felt nervous and awkward as a new hire, but steady about not signing a false date.

qa.q: What did the supervisor do to reinforce Mridul's choice?
qa.a: Backed Mridul to Rafiq, reminded staff to log missed checks without blame, and thanked Mridul at the team meeting.

qa.q: How might Rafiq have felt afterwards?
qa.a: Rafiq was a bit annoyed at first, used to the old way, but may come to see the deviation log as fairer.

grounding: A supervisor records a new hire who declines to backdate a calibration, gives the reason and offers an honest, compliant alternative.

passage:
Tanvir's diary, Wednesday night
Third day at the logistics firm. At four, Naveen, my senior, slid a delivery form across the desk and said, "Just put last Friday's date. The client needs it to show on time." My heart was pounding. Everyone was watching, or it felt like it. I said, "I can't put a date that isn't true. But I can write today's date and add a note saying the shipment was delayed by the port strike, with the port notice attached." Naveen stared at me for a second. Then he sighed and said, "Fine, try it. If the client shouts, you handle it." The client didn't shout. They just said thanks for the explanation.
I'm writing this down so I remember how it felt. Scary, but only for about a minute. If I'd said yes today, I think saying no next month would have been much harder.

qa.q: What did Naveen ask Tanvir to put on the form?
qa.a: Naveen asked Tanvir to put last Friday's date.

qa.q: What was Tanvir feeling when Naveen slid the form across?
qa.a: Tanvir felt nervous, with a pounding heart and the sense that everyone was watching, but was determined to stay honest.

qa.q: Which of Tanvir's choices made refusing work?
qa.a: Tanvir said the reason simply and offered a true alternative, today's date with a delay note and the port notice, so the client still got what they needed.

qa.q: How might Naveen see the new hire after the client's reply?
qa.a: Naveen may feel surprised and perhaps a little respectful, seeing the honest way worked without trouble.

grounding: Shows a new hire declining to backdate a form, giving the reason simply and offering an honest alternative at the first bend.
